title: Mbarara University Research Ethics Education Program
text: Unethical research does not just harm individuals; it erodes public confidence in science, undermines health systems, and corrupts the data that governments rely on to protect their populations, making rigorous ethics training a public health necessity. The MUREEP directly addresses this threat by training a cohort of researchers, ethicists, and research regulators in Uganda, ensuring that NIH-funded studies meet the highest standards of scientific integrity and human protection. As artificial intelligence and emerging health biotechnologies rapidly transform health research and clinical practice, MUREEP equips researchers, REC members and regulators with the knowledge and skills to ensure these innovations are evaluated and implemented in ways that are scientifically sound and ethically grounded in the principles of the Belmont report, the 45 code of federal regulation 46, and the national guidelines.

title: Neural mechanisms of lightness constancy
text:
Because the real-world variables that we care about are entangled in the sensory input, the brain must
disentangle the input to reliably recover those variables (perceptual constancy). The applicant proposes to
study the neural mechanisms underlying a particularly tractable form of perceptual constancy, i.e. lightness
constancy. This research holds significant health relevance because these mechanisms are critical to parse
the complex scenes of natural vision, which is specifically disrupted in visual agnosias, and may inform the
development of visual cortical prostheses that better approach natural vision.

title: Communicating Narrative Concerns Entered by RNs (CONCERN)
text:
In this renewal R01, we will conduct an observational implementation study across 5 health
systems to evaluate the fairness and generalizability of the CONCERN predictive model and
clinical decision support intervention. We will also explore how CONCERN could leverage
pediatric caregiver input in real-time to improve the CONCERN predictive model. In this project
we will also research how social determinants of health data and census level data can improve
the CONCERN model so that it contributes to more equitable care for patients.

title: Community Outreach and Engagement (COE)
text: PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT – COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT Community Outreach and Engagement (COE) at UC San Diego, Moores Cancer Center (MCC) implements initiatives and programs, across the consortium, to reduce the burden of cancer in San Diego County, the MCC catchment area. COE addresses this cancer burden in the catchment area through (1) sustained community partnerships that identify and disseminate evidence-based, cancer-related information and resources across the cancer continuum and (2) integration of knowledge obtained from these efforts into MCC operations. SD County is populated by heterogeneous demographic groups, representing multiple heritages, languages, and traditions. Medicaid-insured individuals make up 40% of the catchment area population (compared to 19% in the United States), most of whom receive primary care at Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs). Under the leadership of the newly appointed (2024) Associate Director (AD) for COE, Jesse Nodora DrPH, with continued support from Assistant Director for COE Corinne McDaniels-Davidson, PhD (San Diego State University), the goal of COE is to reduce the cancer burden and improve health outcomes in the catchment area, guided by the following Aims: Aim 1) Assess and monitor cancer burden in the catchment area; Aim 2) Foster and facilitate research that addresses cancer burden in the catchment area; Aim 3) Conduct cancer outreach and education to reduce the cancer burden in the catchment area; and Aim 4) Engage with regional and national partners to inform decision-making and impact policy. These aims are accomplished in close bidirectional collaboration with the MCC Community Advisory Board (CAB), an Internal Advisory Committee, and a newly established Research Program COE Liaison Committee, which includes representatives from all five MCC Research Programs. Additional collaboration includes the strong partnership with Cancer Research Training and Education Coordination (CRTEC) to align COE initiatives with MCC educational goals. Noteworthy COE accomplishments over this grant period include the following: (1) COE interventions contributing to the rapid return of colorectal cancer screening rates in FQHCs in the catchment area to pre-pandemic rates; (2) increased HPV vaccination rates among 13 to 17-year-old residents; (3) a six-fold increase in MCC funding to COE, enabling the addition of five COE staff; (4) expanded partnerships with regional FQHCs from three to eight health systems, resulting in a Cancer Moonshot grant and four Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA)-funded cancer screening service grants; (5) policy-changing impact in tobacco control, HPV vaccination, biomarker testing, CRC screening, and fertility preservation among young cancer survivors; and (6) an expanded CAB role to include participation in both the MCC Protocol Review and Monitoring Committee and Pilot Grant Review Committee. Plans for the next funding period are to further enhance community outreach in cancer screening and prevention in partnership with a new planned Center for the Early Detection and Prevention of Cancer and to lead community-driven research efforts in partnership with other NCI-Cancer Centers to better inform a national approach to reduce cancer burden.

title: A novel pathway to overcome resistance to immunotherapy in melanoma
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health and the mission of the NIH and NCI because it will test and
define a novel targetable mechanism to overcome resistance and enhance responses to immune checkpoint
inhibitors in melanoma. Thus, these studies will provide the basis for the development of unique combinatorial
approaches to treat patients suffering from melanoma and possibly other cancers.

title: Brain Age in Aphasia
text:
Post-stroke aphasia is a significant public health problem whose symptoms depend on the stroke lesion and on
the status of the surrounding brain tissue. Stroke survivors are at risk for premature brain aging and this project
will evaluate the mechanistic relationship between brain tissue aging, aphasia severity and recovery.

title: LF-TIMING: Large-scale label-free profiling of cell-cell interactions
text:
8. Project Narrative
Advances in computer vision have provided new capabilities for rapid, functional analysis of single cells. We
have used these AI-enabled techniques to profile cells used for immunotherapy to understand which therapies
perform best and why. In this project, we will create a commercially scalable prototype integrated software
system capable of the same analysis on cells that are not fluorescently labelled (label-free). This software will
be based on new AI models trained on millions of images of cells and optimized for fast, high-throughput single
cell analysis by any customer without computational science backgrounds.

title: Jumonji KDM4A drives targetable oncogenic programs in small cell lung cancer
text:
Recently, it has been found that among all FDA approved anti-cancer drugs and hundreds of
investigational drugs under advanced development, none showed a promising profile against
small cell lung cancer cells. We have developed inhibitors of Jumonji demethylases, enzymes
that mediate transcriptional reprogramming during oncogenesis and the development of
therapeutic resistance. These inhibitors kill drug-resistant SCLC cells, so we propose to test their
efficacy against this recalcitrant disease in various in vivo models and to molecularly characterize
their anti-cancer action on the epigenome.

title: Innate Antiviral Signals for Cancer Immunotherapy
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is defined by a deeply immunosuppressive immune infiltrate implicated in intrinsic T cell
ignorance and hindrance of systemic immunotherapy with immune checkpoint blockade. This project will unravel
the mechanisms of local GBM immunotherapy with recombinant poliovirus, PVSRIPO, based on its uniquely
broad and profound proinflammatory effects in the GBM myeloid infiltrate and surrounding brain. This project will
define new therapy paradigms for viral GBM immunotherapy by addressing recently discovered factors in
immunotherapy resistance.

title: Identifying and reducing stigmatizing language in home healthcare: the ENGAGE study
text: Documentation quality in clinical settings varies significantly across patient populations, contributing to health disparities and affecting care delivery for racial and ethnic minority patients. This project aims to design and pilot-test a technology-driven system, ENGAGE, that will help to optimize documentation quality and identify patterns that impact care quality among home healthcare nurses. Achieving this goal will improve the quality of care and reduce health disparities for patients treated in home healthcare settings.

title: Microglia-targeted molecular imaging as a novel biomarker for Alzheimer's disease
text:
Neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s disease (AD) involve chronic brain inflammation driven by immune
cells called microglia. This project aims to develop noninvasive brain imaging tools to study a key microglial
protein, FLAP (encoded by ALOX5AP), which is elevated in AD and may play a role in disease onset and
progression. We will design and evaluate small-molecule compounds that selectively bind FLAP and can be
used for PET brain imaging. These imaging tools will improve our understanding of microglial involvement in AD-
related neuroinflammation and may support the development of future therapies targeting immune pathways in
neurodegeneration.

title: Xenbase: the Xenopus Model Organism Knowledgebase
text:
Component: OVERALL
PROJECT NARRATIVE
Xenbase is the Xenopus model organism knowledgebase, an online resource that integrates, curates,
and disseminates all genomic and biological data from Xenopus research. Our mission is to accelerate
the translation of Xenopus research into knowledge that will improve human health.

title: The Medical Physician Engineers, Scientists, and Clinicians Preparatory Program [MPESC-Prep]
text: The Medical Physician Engineers, Scientists, and Clinicians Preparatory program [MPESC-Prep] (pronounced ‘em-pesk’) will establish a multifaceted training program designed to ensure talented, high school and college students are exposed to opportunities for professional development and mentorship during STEM training to pursue formal education and training in the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular, pulmonary, and hematologic conditions.

title: Single-use Microfluidic Device for Radiopharmaceutical Production
text:
The immense infrastructure, resource, and logistical burdens associated with current radiopharmaceutical
production and distribution limit the proliferation and development of these valuable drugs with
crucial diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities. To address this critical hurdle, we will develop a rapid,
inexpensive microfluidics-based approach for low-cost, dose-on-demand production of human dosage
quantities of ready-to-inject radiopharmaceuticals that can be adapted to a variety of relevant
chemistries. Further, we will develop the proposed platform as a means to simplify raw isotope distribution
logistics by using the chip itself as both the container for shipping and the module for purifying (and
eventually reacting) the desired radiometal.

title: Comparative Analysis of Aneuploidy and Cellular Fragmentation Dynamics in Mammalian Embryos
text:
Reproductive success in several mammalian species is greatly limited by embryo loss due to chromosomal
abnormalities, or aneuploidy. The proposed studies aim to determine the precise relationship between
aneuploidy and a dynamic process called cellular fragmentation that differs in frequency across mammals using
a comparative genomics approach. This work has the potential to improve reproductive efficiency in agriculturally
important animals and for translational application to human assisted reproduction.

title: The CRISPR Vision Program: Nonviral Genome Editing Platforms to Treat Inherited Retinal Channelopathies Epqt Supplement
text:
The goal of this Administrative Supplement application is to secure funding necessary to purchase
a multi-angle dynamic light scattering (MADLS®), which is critical for particle size measurement,
zeta potential measurement, and particle concentration analysis of the lead formulation as the
program transitions into CGMP Manufacturing which is critical for the completion of experiments
detailed in NEI funded U19NS132296, K. Saha PI), entitled The CRISPR Vision Program:
Nonviral Genome Editing Platforms to Treat Inherited Retinal Channelopathies.“

title: Nonterminal Albumin Fusions for Improved Delivery of Polypeptides
text:
This project seeks to enhance the delivery and effectiveness of therapeutic polypeptides, which are vital for
treating a wide range of diseases. By employing both experimental and computational methods, we aim to
optimize the fusion of these polypeptides at nonterminal sites within albumin, a protein that can improve their
stability and targeted delivery. The successful development of these fusions may significantly advance
therapeutic strategies, providing more effective and long-lasting treatment options.

title: Personalized Colorectal Cancer Prevention: Integrating Individual Screening and Follow Up Information with Genetic Data
text:
Although screening colonoscopy can reduce colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence and mortality, there is
considerable variability in individual risk of CRC. Better CRC risk estimates could improve CRC prevention
through personalized approaches to the timing, modality (colonoscopy or non-invasive options) and frequency
of screening and follow up. To achieve this goal, we need risk prediction models that incorporate individual
clinical factors and screening history (if available) with genetic information for each Veteran. This CDA proposal
seeks to build an accurate database of Veterans who developed CRC and advanced precancerous lesions, link
this database to the Million Veteran Program to expand genetic discovery across diverse populations, and create
an equitable tool for personalized assessments of CRC risk. More precise CRC risk stratification will improve
CRC prevention by better targeting colonoscopy resources to the individuals at increased risk for CRC, while
reducing the costs and harms of invasive screening and follow up in those at low risk.

title: Interdisciplinary Training in Auditory Neuroscience
text:
This Interdisciplinary Training Program in Auditory Neuroscience (TPAN) will provide graduate student
training, research experience, and a vibrant community at the interface of neuroscience and
neurotechnology, in both human and animal models. This training program will prepare students for
independent research careers that can improve our understanding of auditory system function and
treatments of auditory system dysfunction using innovative tools and technologies. It is expected that
graduates of this training program will develop creative solutions, devices and strategies to advance
sensory neuroscience and to ultimately assist and prevent hearing loss in human patients.

title: From the Past to the Future: Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells for Lymphoid Malignancies
text:
(PROJECT 1)
The goal of this project is to address major challenges and unmet needs of chimeric antigen receptor or “CAR”
T cells that currently limit treatment success in patients with blood and lymph node cancers. We propose to
identify critical characteristics of effective CAR T cell products to obtain information useful in optimizing therapy
and then engineer around resistance mechanisms using cutting-edge gene editing tools with the goal of creating
CAR T cells more effective at inducing long-lasting remissions. The proposed research is relevant to public health
because it will help increase the potency of CAR T cells used to treat chemotherapy-resistant cancers, which
may make this strategy viable and efficacious for many more patients.
